relations: Hydraulic head descends onto stack top, compressing layers as overall height shrinks.
Protruding left plank holds position while boards above it settle closer together.
Clear plastic wrap on right shifts and crinkles under compression.
Frame, striped columns, and hazard base remain fixed around the pressing zone.
caption: The video captures a hydraulic press head bearing down on a vertical stack of light-colored wooden planks wrapped in clear plastic film. The planks rest on a cylindrical base painted with yellow-and-black hazard stripes. A gray machine frame flanked by striped safety columns and a small action camera on the left surrounds the pressing zone. Over time, the large metallic head descends steadily, its lower rim pressing down onto the top of the stack while the bottom layers remain seated on the base. The overall height of the stack visibly shrinks, the individual boards pressing closer together. The protruding plank on the left side holds roughly its position as the layers above it settle, and the plastic wrap on the right shifts and crinkles. The surrounding frame, columns, and base stay fixed, keeping the view a steady close-up on the compressing wood.
